kitDescription: Miranda is a Fire-element Elysion SMG Supporter on Burst I whose entire kit is team buffing — she deals no skill damage of her own. As she fires, every 30 landed rounds she grants the whole team a small Hit Rate boost, gives an extra Hit Rate boost to allies who also carry submachine guns, and pumps her own ATK by roughly half for a few seconds; at SMG cadence these refresh so often they are effectively always up. Whenever the team enters Full Burst she hands everyone a large Critical Damage boost for the full window, buffs her own Critical Rate and Attack Damage, and drops a huge Critical Rate spike on the single highest-final-ATK ally that lasts only that ally's next round fired. Her own Burst I cast then gives the two highest-final-ATK allies both an ATK and a Critical Damage boost for ten seconds. Net effect: she is a crit-damage and ATK amplifier for whichever teammates hit hardest, with a marginal accuracy assist to the squad's accuracy-circle weapons.

skill1.driverSaid: hitCount 30 / target allies / hitRatePct 5.44 durationSec 5 — newly ENCODED this gauntlet (FIX-A), removed from unmodeled
skill1.blindSaid: S6 identical block; S5 asserts targets == full roster and count == activations × roster size, both GREEN
skill1.formulaCheck: Hit Rate is not a damage bucket — it feeds R(hr) in the UNIGEO accuracy-circle geometry (damage-calculation.md §1b: R(hr) = (CIRCLE_PX_K·scale_w)/2 · (1 − hr/100)), lifting the Core term inside the additive Major bracket for AR/SMG/SG holders only. Routing as a plain hitRatePct stat buff is the engine's sanctioned channel; MG/SR/RL holders correctly see no effect (flat 0.95).
skill1.explanation: Prose value, duration, trigger and target all match. The un-dropping is justified: hard rule 4 gates the MAGNITUDE of the HR→core lift (measured-only), not the existence of the stat, and modernia ships the same stat as of 2026-07-25. The driver flags the magnitude ⚑ with a recipe. Fires ~every 30 landed rounds (≈1.5s at the live 20/s SMG rate) — S5's activation-count band (>10, <400) and the hitCount×2 counterfactual halving confirm real cadence, not a passive.

skill1.driverSaid: alliesOfWeapon weapon SMG / hitRatePct 3.79 durationSec 5 — separate block from the 5.44 line
skill1.blindSaid: S6 identical (alliesOfWeapon SMG); S5 asserts the 3.79 target set contains miranda, excludes helm (SR), and is a strict subset of the 5.44 set — GREEN

skill1.explanation: The weapon scope is preserved as its own block — this is exactly the misread S2b predicted (merging into one unscoped 9.23 all-allies buff) and the driver did NOT make it. Discrimination is on target COUNT, which is correct: in the driver's fixture (crown MG / ada RL / helm SR) the scoped-vs-unscoped damage is byte-identical because HR is inert on non-accuracy-circle weapons, so a damage-delta assertion would have asserted nothing. The driver states this reasoning explicitly in the test header.

skill1.formulaCheck: atkPct is the (1 + Σ ATK%) term on staticAtk inside FinalATK (§1a) — correct bucket for a plain 'ATK ▲ x%' line, distinct from attackDamagePct. Self-only, so it scales only her own small Supporter output (staticAtk 98,367 basis).

Both driver and blind prove the 5s window is genuinely honoured via a shortened-window counterfactual, so the near-permanent uptime is a consequence of cadence, not of an untimed encoding.

skill2.blindSaid: S6 identical; S5 asserts count == FB count and target set == [miranda] — GREEN

skill2.driverSaid: attackDamagePct 23.7 durationSec 10, self, co-resident in the critRate block
skill2.blindSaid: S6 identical stat key and block grouping — GREEN
skill2.formulaCheck: attackDamagePct is the DamageUp bucket (§1e), which MULTIPLIES against the ATK bucket rather than diluting inside it — the bucket distinction the SSOT calls out explicitly (×1.5×1.3 = ×1.95, not +80%). Encoding it as atkPct would be a real bucket error.
skill2.explanation: Correct bucket, and the driver's M5 counterfactual bucket-swaps it to atkPct and proves miranda's damage moves — so the test discriminates the bucket rather than merely observing the value.

skill2.kitLine: FB enter → top-1 final ATK: CR 85.42% 1 round
skill2.driverSaid: alliesTopAtk count 1 / excludeSelf true / byFinalAtk true, critRatePct 85.42 durationShots 1, NO durationSec — re-encoded this gauntlet (FIX-B) from the previously shipped durationSec 1.5
skill2.blindSaid: S6 independently wrote durationShots 1 from the prose alone; S5 asserts every buffApply carries durationShots === 1, targetSlug !== miranda, one per FB, and that forcing durationSec 1 changes team total — GREEN
skill2.formulaCheck: §11: 'for N round(s)' is round-scoped, implemented as durationShots (a round = one bullet, spent right after the shot so the Nth shot still benefits) — categorically NOT a seconds duration. The engine decrements shotsLeft on the HOLDER's shots, so the window rides the recipient's cadence, which is the whole point of the mechanic.
skill2.explanation: This is the highest-value line in the audit and the fix is unambiguously correct. The old durationSec 1.5 was a cadence-dependent fudge: ~1 shot on an SR carry (where it was authored and looked right), ~30 shots on an SMG carry. The driver's own arithmetic (~36×) is in the right order of magnitude; the exact factor depends on the recipient's rate and is immaterial to the ruling. Crucially the driver also asserts expiresFrame is null — a round-count buff must not carry a parallel wall-clock expiry — which is the assertion that would catch a half-migration.

burst.driverSaid: burstCast / alliesTopAtk count 2 excludeSelf byFinalAtk / atkPct 40.4 durationSec 10
burst.blindSaid: S6 identical; S5 asserts 2 distinct non-miranda targets per cast and shared target set with the critDmg sibling — GREEN
burst.formulaCheck: atkPct on the RECIPIENT'S own staticAtk (§1a) — correct. The prose says plain 'ATK ▲ 40.4%', not 'x% of caster's ATK', so casterAtkPct (a flat add of the caster's base ATK, §1a/§11) would be the wrong mechanic and would collapse the buff given miranda's Supporter ATK basis.
burst.explanation: burstCast keying is right: the burst block carries no 'Activates when' clause, so per the classification convention it fires on her own Burst I cast (cd 20s, datamined skill_cooltime 2000). Both effects sit in ONE block so a single target resolution serves both — this is what prevents the ATK grant from re-ranking 'final ATK' before the crit-damage sibling resolves, the trap S2b flagged. The driver's casterAtkPct counterfactual makes the stat choice discriminating rather than assumed.

verdictRationale: No REAL-GOTCHAs. All 9 kit lines are FAITHFUL, unmodeled is legitimately empty for all three slots (this is a pure stat-buff support kit — no damage riders, DoTs, weapon swaps, heals, shields, gauge or ammo lines, so nothing is silently dropped and the FB-timing/noFb and range rules have nothing to apply to). Convergence is strong and, importantly, cross-fixture rather than merely cross-agent: the S5 blind tests ran a DIFFERENT comp (liter/crown/miranda/helm, two Burst I units) from the driver's (miranda/crown/ada/helm, sole Burst I), and every shared assertion was green — the two-B1 fixture is precisely the one that separates fullBurstEnter from burstCast on skill2, so that trigger split is corroborated by a fixture the driver did not use. The S6 blind override is semantically identical to the shipped one including both of this gauntlet's fixes. The two fixes rank as: (1) FIX-B, the '1 round(s)' → durationShots 1 re-encoding, is the substantive win — the prior durationSec 1.5 was a cadence-dependent over-credit (roughly right on an SR carry, an order of magnitude wrong on a fast-firing one), and §11's round-scoped rule plus the helm '10 round(s)' precedent make the round-count reading mandatory, not preferential; the driver additionally pins expiresFrame === null so a half-migration cannot pass. (2) FIX-A, un-dropping the two Hit Rate lines, is correctly reasoned: hard rule 4 gates the MAGNITUDE of the HR→core lift, not the stat's existence, hitRatePct is live-wired for accuracy-circle weapons via acrForHR/UNIGEO, and modernia already ships the same stat. Discrimination holds throughout — the load-bearing counterfactuals (hitCount×2 halving the activation count, self-vs-allies retargeting on three separate lines, attackDamagePct-vs-atkPct bucket swap, atkPct-vs-casterAtkPct, durationShots-vs-durationSec, count 1-vs-2) each move an observable, and where a damage delta would be vacuous (the SMG weapon scope, inert on the fixture's MG/RL/SR allies) the driver correctly discriminates on target count instead and says so. Three same-model residuals for the owner to spot-check, none blocking: (a) the HR→core magnitude is derived, not measured — the additive-in-pp composition of 5.44 + 3.79 into one R(hr) is UNVALIDATED (R8) and every agent here inherited the same assumption, so the recipe in the override note (CORE HIT popup fraction inside vs outside the ~5s post-30-hit window in a miranda focus video, on an AR/SMG/SG ally) is the real confirmation; (b) hitCount:30 is keyed to LANDED rounds per the prose 'after landing 30' — if in-game SMG landing fraction is below 1 the true proc interval is longer than the sim's, which the S6 caveat flags and nobody measured; note also that the live SMG rate is the frame-quantized 20/s, not the nominal 24/s, so the ~1.5s cadence figure is the correct one; (c) byFinalAtk (live effectiveAtk ranking) on all three highest-final-ATK targets is the literal-prose reading and all three agents agreed, but both blinds explicitly declared the static-vs-live ranking NOT discriminable in their fixtures — so it is convergent-by-reading, not proven by test. That last point is a coverage gap, not a defect, and does not gate GO.
